commit.message:
eink0rn: bump to v1.1.6 (#205)

Bumps `checkers/eink0rn.yaml` from v1.1.5 to v1.1.6. One change, to the
memo tables: they are now split on whether the term mentions a local
constant, and the closed half is left unbounded. That is what
`magma-string-pair-n9` wanted — it was the one decline of the last round
and is now checked in seconds — and it leaves `con-leche` alone, whose
hard declaration reduces under binders and so stays in the bounded half.

Also puts the timeout back to 10 minutes. Five was enough for everything
that finishes (mathlib 4.3 m, con-leche 4.0 m in the 2026-09-13 round)
but left under a minute of headroom on a shared runner.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit.diff:
@@ -3,7 +3,7 @@
 # in there -- a file cannot name the commit that contains it -- so the copy in
 # checkers/eink0rn.yaml carries the commit `ref` points at, put in on the way:
 #
-#   sed "s|^rev: .*|rev: $(git rev-parse v1.1.5^{commit})|" \
+#   sed "s|^rev: .*|rev: $(git rev-parse v1.1.6^{commit})|" \
 #     tools/arena-checker.yaml > ../lean-kernel-arena/checkers/eink0rn.yaml
 #
 # The pattern is anchored so that this line is not itself rewritten.
@@ -28,10 +28,10 @@ description: |
   including the one `--enforce-mutual-univ` turns off below, so that the
   language scored here is the language every other checker is scored on.
   Nothing is declined; the largest export peaks around eight gigabytes.
-version: "1.1.5"
+version: "1.1.6"
 url: https://github.com/Timeroot/eink0rn
-ref: v1.1.5
-rev: 31a9e3a1347d0544e8362fabea0ac669b41afbbb
+ref: v1.1.6
+rev: ca5c1d24691011daba4c064f989f18d2d16cabd1
 threads: 8
 build: bash tools/arena-build.sh
 # Exit codes are the arena's: 0 accept, 1 reject, 2 declined, 3 a fault in the
@@ -77,16 +77,18 @@ build: bash tools/arena-build.sh
 #               are what the old generation has to absorb.
 #
 # The timeout is the same idea for the clock: a decline, not a wrong answer,
-# and not a job that runs the matrix out of its 360 minutes.  mathlib took 15
-# minutes of it on a box under other load; every other export is minutes.
+# and not a job that runs the matrix out of its 360 minutes.  Ten minutes is
+# about twice the slowest export on this runner -- in the round of 2026-09-13,
+# mathlib 4.3 minutes and con-leche 4.0 -- so reaching it means a file that was
+# not going to finish.
 #
 # The two rewritten statuses are both resource limits reported as such.  124 is
 # the timeout above.  251 is the RTS's own heap-limit exit, taken when the live
 # set grows so fast between two collections that the limit is passed by more
 # than the grace the handler needs to print DECLINE itself; either way -M did
 # its job, and neither is a judgement about the file.
 run: |
-  timeout 300 ./arena/eink0rn --enforce-mutual-univ --mem=4000 -j8 "$IN" \
+  timeout 600 ./arena/eink0rn --enforce-mutual-univ --mem=4000 -j8 "$IN" \
     +RTS -A32m -M13g -RTS
   rc=$?
   case $rc in
